Event date 2015-10-15 (Obama announced 9,800 troops kept through most of 2016, drawdown to 5,500 in 2017). Window used: Oct 15 to Oct 29, 2015.

Press: 10 items, 8 fetched directly, 2 (Daily Signal, Stabroek) from search results only. Opinion pieces are filed under kind "press" because the schema allows only press or tweet; item_type marks them. No Guardian, BBC, Al Jazeera, WSJ, National Review, or The Nation item from the window was found. The National Review hit was undated and about 2016; The Nation hit was from 2014. Fetch failures excluded: Win Without War (403), Washington Times (403), Christian Today (404, title only).

Poll: no Gallup, Pew, or CNN poll from the window found. Gallup hits were 2009. AP-GfK poll is dated Nov 5, 2015, outside window. YouGov Oct 15 2015 item: fetch 404, topline not retrieved, excluded. Breitbart Oct 20 2015 poll write-up: title only, figures unverified, excluded.

Twitter: NONE evidenced. Search summaries quoted a Kevin McCarthy tweet (@GOPLeader, Oct 15 2015) and a Mike Huckabee tweet, but no tweet URL or fetched article quoting them was found in the window, so both excluded. The turnto23 McCarthy article quotes a statement with an embedded tweet dated July 6, 2016, so it is not evidence for Oct 2015. Sen. McCain's reaction was a written statement, not a tweet.

Stance here is toward the decision as written, not wider coalition or media overlay analysis.

events.notes:
Event: Obama announced July 6, 2016 that about 8,400 troops stay through end of term (replacing planned 5,500 by end-2016). Window used: July 6-20, 2016.
Press: 10 items, all from fetched pages. Items 1-10 are real and dated within window. Left/center/right covered; international covered (Dawn, Express Tribune, Al Jazeera). Not found: NYT, WaPo, WSJ, Guardian, BBC, National Review, Reuters/AP as fetchable items; a pass on these outlets by name was not reached. Poll: none found in Pew/Gallup/CNN searches.
Blocked (403) and not used: Bloomberg ("Obama Finds He Can't Escape Afghan War He Once Vowed to End", headline seen in search results only), Washington Times, Daily Signal, Win Without War.
Twitter: only 1 tweet evidenced (Mujahid, via Express Tribune quote). Unverified claims seen only in search-result summaries, not on fetched pages, so excluded: Ashraf Ghani welcome tweet (Tribune article fetched describes a palace statement, not a tweet), NATO Stoltenberg "strong signal" tweet (exact phrase not found), McCain tweet (Breaking Defense quotes a statement, not a tweet), White House @POTUS tweet. Mujahid is a Taliban spokesman, not a member of Congress, journalist or US official; included as an official spokesperson.
Coordination/overlay analysis was not performed by this subagent.
